Exercise 15.8.26 — Volume Cut Out by a Cylinder (Cylindrical Coordinates)

Problem. Use cylindrical coordinates.

(a) Find the volume of the solid that the cylinder r=acos⁡θr = a\cos\thetar=acosθ cuts out of the sphere of radius aaa centered at the origin.

(b) Illustrate the solid of part (a) by graphing the sphere and the cylinder on the same screen.

Notation used in this solution

SymbolMeaning
(r,θ,z)(r,\theta,z)(r,θ,z) Cylindrical coordinates: x=rcos⁡θx = r\cos\thetax=rcosθ, y=rsin⁡θy = r\sin\thetay=rsinθ, so x2+y2=r2x^2+y^2 = r^2x2+y2=r2 and dV=r dz dr dθdV = r\,dz\,dr\,d\thetadV=rdzdrdθ.
aaa The common size parameter: radius of the sphere and scale of the cylinder. It is a positive constant, a>0a > 0a>0.
r=acos⁡θr = a\cos\thetar=acosθ The cylinder. Since x2+y2=r2=arcos⁡θ=axx^2+y^2 = r^2 = a r\cos\theta = a xx2+y2=r2=arcosθ=ax, in Cartesian form it is x2+y2=axx^2 + y^2 = a xx2+y2=ax, i.e. (x−a/2)2+y2=a2/4(x - a/2)^2 + y^2 = a^2/4(x−a/2)2+y2=a2/4: the surface of revolution about the zzz-axis of the circle of radius a/2a/2a/2 centered at (a/2,0,0)(a/2, 0, 0)(a/2,0,0).
Viviani solid / Viviani curve The solid cut out of the sphere by the cylinder is the classical Viviani solid. Its boundary curve r=acos⁡θ,  z=±asin⁡θr = a\cos\theta,\; z = \pm a\sin\thetar=acosθ,z=±asinθ is the Viviani curve.

Part 1 — Volume of the solid (part (a))

Step 1.1: Describe the region in cylindrical coordinates.

The sphere has equation x2+y2+z2=a2x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = a^2x2+y2+z2=a2, i.e. r2+z2=a2r^2 + z^2 = a^2r2+z2=a2. The cylinder is r=acos⁡θr = a\cos\thetar=acosθ. Its interior is 0≤r≤acos⁡θ0 \le r \le a\cos\theta0≤r≤acosθ, which is nonempty exactly where cos⁡θ≥0\cos\theta \ge 0cosθ≥0, i.e. −π/2≤θ≤π/2-\pi/2 \le \theta \le \pi/2−π/2≤θ≤π/2. Inside the cylinder the sphere gives −a2−r2≤z≤a2−r2-\sqrt{a^2 - r^2} \le z \le \sqrt{a^2 - r^2}−a2−r2​≤z≤a2−r2​. Hence

V=∫−π/2π/2∫0acos⁡θ∫−a2−r2a2−r2r dz dr dθ. V = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \int_0^{a\cos\theta} \int_{-\sqrt{a^2-r^2}}^{\sqrt{a^2-r^2}} r\, dz\, dr\, d\theta. V=∫−π/2π/2​∫0acosθ​∫−a2−r2​a2−r2​​rdzdrdθ.

Step 1.2: Integrate with respect to zzz.

∫−a2−r2a2−r2r dz=2a2−r2  r. \int_{-\sqrt{a^2-r^2}}^{\sqrt{a^2-r^2}} r\,dz = 2\sqrt{a^2-r^2}\,\, r. ∫−a2−r2​a2−r2​​rdz=2a2−r2​r.

Because the integrand is even in θ\thetaθ and the interval [0,acos⁡θ][0, a\cos\theta][0,acosθ] is symmetric in the same sense, we may integrate θ\thetaθ from 000 to π/2\pi/2π/2 and double:

V=2∫0π/2∫0acos⁡θ2a2−r2 r dr dθ. V = 2 \int_0^{\pi/2} \int_0^{a\cos\theta} 2\sqrt{a^2-r^2}\, r\, dr\, d\theta. V=2∫0π/2​∫0acosθ​2a2−r2​rdrdθ.

Step 1.3: Evaluate the rrr-integral by the substitution r=asin⁡ur = a\sin ur=asinu.

With r=asin⁡ur = a\sin ur=asinu, dr=acos⁡u dudr = a\cos u\,dudr=acosudu, and on 0≤u≤π/20 \le u \le \pi/20≤u≤π/2 we have a2−r2=acos⁡u\sqrt{a^2 - r^2} = a\cos ua2−r2​=acosu. The upper limit r=acos⁡θr = a\cos\thetar=acosθ corresponds to u=π/2−θu = \pi/2 - \thetau=π/2−θ. Therefore

∫0acos⁡θ2a2−r2 r dr=∫0π/2−θ2a3sin⁡ucos⁡2u du=2a33(1−sin⁡3θ). \int_0^{a\cos\theta} 2\sqrt{a^2-r^2}\, r\, dr = \int_0^{\pi/2-\theta} 2a^3 \sin u \cos^2 u\, du = \frac{2a^3}{3}\left(1 - \sin^3\theta\right). ∫0acosθ​2a2−r2​rdr=∫0π/2−θ​2a3sinucos2udu=32a3​(1−sin3θ).

Indeed, ∫0csin⁡u cos⁡2u du=−13cos⁡3u∣0c=13(1−cos⁡3c)\int_0^c \sin u\,\cos^2 u\,du = -\frac{1}{3}\cos^3 u\bigg|_0^c = \frac{1}{3}\left(1 - \cos^3 c\right)∫0c​sinucos2udu=−31​cos3u​0c​=31​(1−cos3c), and with c=π/2−θc = \pi/2 - \thetac=π/2−θ we have cos⁡c=cos⁡(π/2−θ)=sin⁡θ\cos c = \cos(\pi/2 - \theta) = \sin\thetacosc=cos(π/2−θ)=sinθ, which gives the displayed value.

Step 1.4: Evaluate the θ\thetaθ-integral.

V=2∫0π/22a33(1−sin⁡3θ)dθ=4a33[∫0π/2dθ−∫0π/2sin⁡3θ dθ]. V = 2 \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{2a^3}{3} \left(1 - \sin^3\theta\right) d\theta = \frac{4a^3}{3}\left[ \int_0^{\pi/2} d\theta - \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^3\theta\, d\theta \right]. V=2∫0π/2​32a3​(1−sin3θ)dθ=34a3​[∫0π/2​dθ−∫0π/2​sin3θdθ].

The two elementary integrals are ∫0π/2dθ=π/2\int_0^{\pi/2} d\theta = \pi/2∫0π/2​dθ=π/2 and ∫0π/2sin⁡3θ dθ=2/3\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^3\theta\,d\theta = 2/3∫0π/2​sin3θdθ=2/3, so

V=4a33(π2−23)=2a39 (3π−4). V = \frac{4a^3}{3}\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{2a^3}{9}\,(3\pi - 4). V=34a3​(2π​−32​)=92a3​(3π−4).

Result (part (a)). V=2a39 (3π−4)≈1.205506 a3. V = \frac{2a^3}{9}\,(3\pi - 4) \approx 1.205506\, a^3. V=92a3​(3π−4)≈1.205506a3. For a=1a = 1a=1: V≈1.20551V \approx 1.20551V≈1.20551; for a=2a = 2a=2: V≈9.64405V \approx 9.64405V≈9.64405.

Step 1.5: Verification by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py reproduces the chain above with SymPy (substitution, outer integral) and then checks the result two independent ways at high precision: a direct mpmath quadrature of the original iterated integral (agrees to about 10−810^{-8}10−8, limited by the square-root cusp at r→ar \to ar→a) and the same quadrature on the smooth substituted integrand (agrees to 10−1410^{-14}10−14). A plain numpy midpoint sum over the 3-D region agrees to 5×10−45\times10^{-4}5×10−4. The figure script part1_figure1.py produces Fig. 1.

Part 2 — Illustration (part (b))

Step 2.1: Graph the sphere and the cylinder together.

With a=1a = 1a=1 the cylinder r=cos⁡θr = \cos\thetar=cosθ is x2+y2=xx^2 + y^2 = xx2+y2=x, the circle of radius 1/21/21/2 centered at (1/2,0)(1/2, 0)(1/2,0) revolved about the zzz-axis. Fig. 2 shows the sphere and the cylinder on the same screen; the orange curve is their intersection. The script part2_step1.py verifies this intersection symbolically-numeric: on it, r=cos⁡θr = \cos\thetar=cosθ and r2+z2=1r^2 + z^2 = 1r2+z2=1, hence z2=1−cos⁡2θ=sin⁡2θz^2 = 1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\thetaz2=1−cos2θ=sin2θ, i.e. the Viviani curve r=cos⁡θ,  z=±sin⁡θr = \cos\theta,\; z = \pm\sin\thetar=cosθ,z=±sinθ.
